SL 4.4.intro: Set a correlation and the page draws 20 students with exactly that $r$. The regression line always passes through the mean point $(\bar{x},\bar{y})$.
SL 4.4.story: Twenty students: hours of revision (across) and test score out of 100 (up).

SL 4.10.intro: Click the grid to add a point; drag a point to move it. Compare Pearson's $r$, which measures a straight line, with Spearman's $r_s$, which only asks whether the pattern always rises or always falls.

presets.label: Linear
presets.story: A straight-line pattern: $r$ and $r_s$ are both close to 1.

presets.label: Curved
presets.story: Hours of typing practice (across) and errors in a test (up), as on the SL 4.10 worked example. Always decreasing, but curved.

presets.label: Outlier
presets.story: Seven points on a rising line and one extreme point. $r$ drops because the point is far from the line; $r_s$ stays at 1 because the point is still ranked last. Drag it below its neighbours and watch $r_s$ move.

presets.label: U shape
presets.story: Falls, then rises. Neither coefficient sees this pattern.

AHL 4.13.intro: Pick a data set, then try models. Each fit shows $R^2$, $SS_{res}$, and the MSE. Decide which model you would use before you press Reveal.

sets.label: Taxi fares
sets.reason: The fare grows by about the same amount for each extra kilometre, so a straight line fits, and a fixed starting fare explains the intercept. The curved models add parameters but barely lower $SS_{res}$.

sets.label: Thrown ball
sets.reason: Under gravity the height rises, peaks, and falls symmetrically: a quadratic. The cubic fits about as closely, but its extra term has no physical meaning.

sets.label: Video views
sets.reason: The views grow by about the same factor (about 1.6) each day, which is exponential growth. A cubic can follow these seven points, but it would turn down outside them.

sets.label: Pendulum
sets.reason: A power model $T=aL^b$ with $b$ close to 0.5 matches the physics: the period grows with the square root of the length, and $T=0$ when $L=0$.

sets.label: Tide height
sets.reason: Tides rise and fall in a repeating cycle, about every 12.5 hours. Only the sine model repeats; every polynomial runs off to infinity outside the data.

sets.label: Seedling height
sets.reason: The plant grows slowly, then quickly, then levels off near its full height of about 60 cm. The logistic model has that ceiling; the cubic scores a similar $R^2$ but would keep growing, or shrink, after week 14.

AHL 4.13.intro: Take logs of one or both variables and watch the axes pull in. When the points fall on a straight line, the line's equation turns back into the model.

sets.label: Video views
sets.story: Total views of a video at the end of each day after it was posted. Which log button makes the points line up?

sets.label: Pendulum
sets.story: The period of a pendulum for nine lengths of string. This one needs both buttons.

sets.label: Vocabulary
sets.story: Words a student remembers after studying a list for different lengths of time. Here only one of the logs helps.
